description: Pins the end-to-end recovery composition protocol::phrase::normalize_user_phrase (§7.4) -> protocol::derive_recovery_wrap_key_from_normalized (§3.1): a raw user-typed 24-word phrase is NFKD-normalized then fed DIRECTLY to Argon2id (NOT BIP-39's PBKDF2 step). 3 cases type the SAME 24 words three ways (canonical / mixed-case+messy-whitespace / NFKD-foldable full-width+exotic-whitespace); all three MUST derive the identical wrap key, pinning the NFKD-before-Argon2id ordering. EXPECTED RUNTIME: ~9s total (~3s per case at canonical params m=256 MiB, t=3, p=2). Default-on in `cargo test`; only the regenerator is `#[ignore]`-gated. Cases generated by `cargo test -p protocol --lib emit_bip39_recovery_vectors_for_paste -- --ignored` (in protocol/src/kdf.rs).

cases.description: The canonical BIP-39 all-zero-entropy 24-word phrase (23x abandon + checksum word 'art'), typed already in normalized form (lowercase, single ASCII spaces, no padding). Baseline: normalize_user_phrase is a fixed point here, so this pins the recovery_wrap_key for the canonical normalized string fed straight to Argon2id.

The SAME 24 words, fully UPPERCASED, with leading/trailing whitespace padding and irregular interior whitespace (double space + tab between every word). normalize_user_phrase ASCII-lowercases, coalesces whitespace runs to a single U+0020, and trims — yielding the identical normalized string as the canonical case, hence the IDENTICAL wrap key. Pins that case-folding + whitespace normalization happen BEFORE Argon2id.

The SAME 24 words, but the checksum word 'art' typed in full-width Latin (U+FF41 U+FF52 U+FF54) and two word separators replaced by a no-break space (U+00A0) and an ideographic space (U+3000). NFKD compatibility-decomposition folds the full-width letters to ASCII and both exotic spaces to regular spaces; the result normalizes to the canonical phrase and derives the IDENTICAL wrap key. Pins NFKD-before-Argon2id: a port that skips the NFKD pass would feed the raw full-width/NBSP bytes to Argon2id and derive a DIFFERENT (wrong) key.
